BatchCreateCampaignAsset.name: BatchCreateCampaignAsset
BatchCreateCampaignAsset.documentation:
Instantiates one or more of the campaign template's blueprints as assets of this campaign.

The only asset-create operation: DG-038 deleted the singular CreateCampaignAsset, and AWS Batch Operations makes exposing a singular alongside a batch optional ("which MAY actually be exposed in addition"). It also replaced kit instantiation -- CreateCampaign creates zero assets, so this is the only path by which an asset comes into existence.

Errors here are whole-request only, and nothing is written when one is thrown. Per-entry failures ride in the response's Errors list with a 200. ServiceQuotaExceededException is deliberately absent: a campaign holds at most one asset per blueprint (I-15), so the ceiling is the size of the bound kit and a request of unique valid entries cannot exceed it.

CreateCampaign.name: CreateCampaign
CreateCampaign.documentation:
Creates a new marketing campaign.

Returns the identity of the new campaign, not the campaign. Growing a response is backward compatible and shrinking one is not, and the caller's next step is a GetCampaign anyway — a write that supplies an audience cannot report its scan verdict, because that is decided after it commits.

CreateSocialConnectionAuthorizationUrl.name: CreateSocialConnectionAuthorizationUrl
CreateSocialConnectionAuthorizationUrl.documentation: Creates a single-use URL the partner visits to authorize publishing on a platform. Serves a first connect, connecting a further account, and re-authorizing an expired one: consenting with an account that is already connected re-authorizes that connection and keeps its id; any other account adds a connection. Poll ListSocialConnections for the outcome. Deliberately not idempotent and takes no client token: every call must mint a fresh single-use URL, so replaying a cached response would hand back a dead one.

DeactivateCampaignAsset.name: DeactivateCampaignAsset
DeactivateCampaignAsset.documentation:
Stops a live campaign asset: an email's scheduled send is withdrawn, a social post is removed before it publishes. On a completed campaign, it also removes a published document, banner or landing page.

Synchronous, and safe to repeat. Does not delete the asset record, so a stopped email or social post can be started again.

Not every asset can be stopped, and the reasons differ in kind. An email that has begun sending cannot be recalled: the send is gone. A document, a banner or a landing page is refused with ASSET_NOT_DEACTIVATABLE until the campaign has completed (the UTC date is after its EndOn). Until then the partner fixes one in place by updating it and activating it again, which keeps its URL, so every email that already linked to it keeps working.

Once the campaign has completed, the removal is permanent, because a completed campaign can't activate anything again:

  • A document's published PDF is deleted. Its URL stops serving within about a minute (the CDN revalidates), and PublicUrl is no longer returned. Anything that linked to it, such as a landing page's download button or a sent email, reaches an error page. The export still contains the document.
  • A banner's or landing page's published object is taken down at the delivery platform, and the images the partner put on it are deleted. A landing page stops capturing leads, and its PublicUrl is no longer returned. A partner site that embedded a banner shows nothing there. The platform's own CDN can keep serving a copy a visitor already cached, which collects nothing.

A landing page and a document it links to can be removed in either order.

DeleteCampaign.name: DeleteCampaign
DeleteCampaign.documentation:
Permanently deletes a campaign, its assets and their stored files.

A hard delete with no undo: the campaign leaves ListCampaigns and every read of it returns ResourceNotFoundException. Its tags are removed with it.

Refused with ConflictException while the campaign has a live asset (CAMPAIGN_HAS_ACTIVE_ASSETS), because deleting the record would orphan what the delivery platform still serves or sends: deactivate those assets first. Also refused while an activation task is running (CAMPAIGN_ACTIVATION_IN_PROGRESS). A completed campaign can be deleted.

Idempotent in effect: deleting a campaign that is already gone returns ResourceNotFoundException, and nothing is left behind by a retry.

DeleteSocialConnection.name: DeleteSocialConnection
DeleteSocialConnection.documentation: Revokes and deletes one social connection; other connections on the same platform are untouched. Idempotent: deleting an unknown or already-deleted connection succeeds rather than returning a not-found error.

GetCampaignAssetActivationTask.name: GetCampaignAssetActivationTask
GetCampaignAssetActivationTask.documentation:
Reads a campaign's current activation task.

Keyed on the campaign, with no task identifier, because a campaign has at most one activation task: runs are serialised, so there is no collection to address into. The caller always holds the task id anyway, because Start returned it — the id is a correlation value, not an address.

Returns the campaign's most recent task. A new task overwrites the previous one, so this is not a history: the durable per-asset record is on the assets themselves. Returns ResourceNotFoundException when the campaign has never had a task, or when its last one has expired.

GetCampaignAssetExportTask.name: GetCampaignAssetExportTask
GetCampaignAssetExportTask.documentation:
Retrieves a campaign asset export task by its identifier, reporting its status and, when the task is COMPLETED, a freshly minted short-lived presigned URL for downloading the ZIP archive.

The download URL is minted on each call and is valid for at most 15 minutes; clients should download promptly rather than caching it. When the task has FAILED, FailureReason explains why. Poll this operation (roughly every 2-5 seconds) until the task reaches a terminal state.

GetCampaignTemplate.name: GetCampaignTemplate
GetCampaignTemplate.documentation: Retrieves full detail of one campaign template, including its ordered asset templates with their field schema and layout previews.

ListCampaignAssets.name: ListCampaignAssets
ListCampaignAssets.documentation: Lists assets for a campaign with pagination.

ListCampaigns.name: ListCampaigns
ListCampaigns.documentation: Lists campaigns with optional filters and pagination.

ListSocialConnections.name: ListSocialConnections
ListSocialConnections.documentation: Lists the partner's social connections, optionally filtered by platform.

ListTagsForResource.name: ListTagsForResource
ListTagsForResource.documentation: Lists the tags applied to a Partner Central Marketing resource.

SearchCampaignTemplates.name: SearchCampaignTemplates
SearchCampaignTemplates.documentation: Searches and browses the AWS-authored campaign template catalog. With no SearchText it returns the whole catalog in the default order, so browse and keyword search share one shape; GetCampaignTemplate reads one template.

StartCampaignAssetActivationTask.name: StartCampaignAssetActivationTask
StartCampaignAssetActivationTask.documentation:
Activates 1–25 of a campaign's assets as one ordered unit, and returns a task to poll.

Takes a list because the service owns the ordering. Assets link to one another by URL — an email's call-to-action carries the landing page's URL, the landing page's download field carries the document's — and a URL does not exist until the asset it points at is activated. Those edges are derived by the service from the campaign's pinned template, so reconstructing and topologically sorting them is work the service has already done, and getting it wrong arms an email with a dead link. Name every asset you want live and the service sequences them; "activate everything" is the list with every id in it, which ListCampaignAssets already gave you.

Asynchronous, because activating an asset installs or arms behaviour that runs later and an email activation bulk-loads its audience into the delivery platform. Everything decidable without a write to the delivery platform is evaluated before this returns; everything else lands on the task.

A refusal that applies to one asset does not fail the request: that asset is on the task already FAILED, with its reason, and the rest run. A refusal that applies to the whole request — a malformed list, an unknown campaign, another task already running on this campaign, this service's service-linked role being deleted (ConflictException SERVICE_LINKED_ROLE_DELETION_IN_PROGRESS), a campaign setting an asset in the request needs (ValidationException CAMPAIGN_INCOMPLETE), a campaign sender that no longer passes CreateCampaign's sender rules while the request names an email (ValidationException with no FieldList, whose message ends with one Reason: <code> token per failed rule: PATTERN_MISMATCH, SENDER_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLIANCE_LEAD, or SENDER_DOMAIN_DKIM_MISSING and/or SENDER_DOMAIN_DMARC_MISSING) — is thrown, and nothing starts.

One task runs on a campaign at a time. A second concurrent call is refused with ConflictException / CAMPAIGN_ACTIVATION_IN_PROGRESS, whose ResourceId names the task already holding the campaign. Two tasks over disjoint asset sets are refused too: the guard is deliberately campaign-wide, because overlapping runs made the per-asset status misleading rather than merely contended.

StartCampaignAssetExportTask.name: StartCampaignAssetExportTask
StartCampaignAssetExportTask.documentation:
Starts an asynchronous task that packages a campaign's assets into a single downloadable ZIP archive.

Fire-and-return: the campaign is validated (it must exist and not be cancelled), a task record is persisted, an asynchronous execution is started, and the task id is returned with status IN_PROGRESS. This operation does not inspect assets — all resolution, exclusion, and failure are determined by the execution and surfaced only by GetCampaignAssetExportTask.

Every campaign is exportable, including one never activated, because renderable assets are composed on demand at export time rather than requiring finished, launched deliverables.

TagResource.name: TagResource
TagResource.documentation:
Adds or replaces tags on a Partner Central Marketing resource.

Idempotent: applying a tag that is already present with the same value is a no-op, and supplying a key that already exists replaces its value.

UntagResource.name: UntagResource
UntagResource.documentation:
Removes tags from a Partner Central Marketing resource.

Idempotent: removing a key that is not present succeeds.

UpdateCampaign.name: UpdateCampaign
UpdateCampaign.documentation:
Edits a campaign in place.

Partial update: an omitted field is left unchanged, which is the standard meaning of an Update verb — a full replacement would be a Put. Change-only, with no way to clear a field back to empty, because the campaign's file members cannot round-trip: they are written as an s3:// reference and read back as a URL or as metadata, so a replacement payload could not resend an unchanged recipient list without re-uploading it.

Refused while an activation task runs (CAMPAIGN_ACTIVATION_IN_PROGRESS) and once the campaign is completed (CAMPAIGN_COMPLETED, the UTC date is after its EndOn).

Last-writer-wins, with no concurrency token: this is low-contention metadata owned by one partner.

UpdateCampaignAsset.name: UpdateCampaignAsset
UpdateCampaignAsset.documentation: Updates an asset's field values, layout or send time. Refused with ConflictException while the campaign's running activation task still owns the asset (ASSET_START_IN_PROGRESS), and for a live email or social post (ASSET_ALREADY_ACTIVE): deactivate it first.

Reason.documentation: Why the caller was refused, when the refusal is about the caller's Partner Central state rather than IAM.

AccessDeniedException.documentation:
You do not have sufficient access to perform this action.

An IAM denial carries no Reason. A refusal for the caller's Partner Central state carries one, so a client tells the two apart by its presence.

AccessDeniedExceptionReason.documentation: Why an AccessDeniedException was raised, when it isn't IAM's.

Code.documentation: What is wrong. Branch on this, not on Message.

FieldId.documentation: The asset field to fix. Present for asset-level issues, except SEND_MODE_MISSING and a CONTENT_REJECTED that refused the asset's text as a whole rather than one field.

CampaignSetting.documentation: The UpdateCampaign member to set. Present for campaign-level issues.

PartnerProfileField.documentation: The partner-profile value to set or shorten, in AWS Partner Central, or the derived value whose input it is. Present on PARTNER_PROFILE_FIELD_MISSING and PARTNER_PROFILE_FIELD_DOES_NOT_FIT.

Message.documentation: A description for display. Don't parse it.

ActivationIssue.documentation: One thing that must be fixed before activation.

ActivationIssueList.documentation: An asset's activation issues; empty when it is ready. At most one per pinned field, so bounded by the field list's own 150.

AllowedTagList.documentation: The HTML tags permitted in a rich-text value.

Amount.documentation: A decimal amount. Accepts "100", "100.5", or "100.00". A string, not a float, because a budget is exact and binary floating point cannot represent every two-decimal value.

AssetLanguage.documentation:
A language a campaign is written and typeset in, as a BCP 47 tag.

A closed set rather than a free string: each value is one DG can render, and a document needs a font for it, so a tag outside the set could not be honoured.

Category.documentation: The category of asset the field may name. The value must be an asset of this category on the same campaign; list the candidates with ListCampaignAssets.

LabelFieldId.documentation: The text field on the same asset whose copy names the linked asset, such as the "Solution Brief" in "Your Solution Brief is ready to download!". When the partner picks an asset, fill this field with the picked asset's LinkLabel, in a preview and in the same save, unless the partner has edited it. The field stays editable. The service does the same when a save changes the link without setting this field and the partner has never written it.

AttemptStatus.documentation:
How the most recent attempt at something ended.

`Status` rather than `State` because each of these describes the progress of a process — an edit, a hand-over to the delivery platform — rather than a resource's lifecycle. The resource's lifecycle is `State`, and it is a separate member.

Named for the attempt — *how did the last attempt at this end?* — and not for the thing attempted, so a second attempt axis can share it rather than copy it.

A member of this type is **omitted before the first attempt**: absence means "never tried", which is a third answer and not a fourth value.

AuthorizationUrl.documentation: Single-use URL the partner visits to grant authorization on the social platform. Returned only by CreateSocialConnectionAuthorizationUrl, never by a read operation. Treated as sensitive: it is a bearer capability, so anyone holding it before it is used can link an account. Never log it.

AwsServiceFilterList.documentation: The AWS-service facet. Values are OR-ed; exact, case-sensitive match.

BatchCreateCampaignAssetEntries.documentation: Bounded per AWS Batch Operations: a batch operation MUST have a documented finite upper limit, and the limit counts entries so a caller can compute it without serializing. 25 matches CampaignAssetTemplateList's own bound -- a kit cannot hold more blueprints than one call can instantiate.

SourceAssetTemplateIdentifier.documentation:
The asset template to instantiate, as returned by GetCampaignTemplate in CampaignTemplate.AssetTemplates[].id.

Must belong to the campaign's own campaign template. An asset's editable field schema is copied from this blueprint at creation and pinned, so an asset without one could be neither validated on update nor made live.

Also this entry's request identifier: it MUST be unique across the request's entries, since a campaign holds at most one asset per blueprint (I-15) and two entries naming the same blueprint could not both succeed.

BatchCreateCampaignAssetEntry.documentation:
One blueprint to instantiate.

Carries nothing but the blueprint's identity, and that is the point rather than a saving: category, name, FileFormat and platform are all derived from the named blueprint, so no caller has a member with which to contradict the pinned schema (asset design section 3.1).

There is deliberately no per-entry ClientToken. AWS Batch Operations requires a request identifier per entry -- "a request identifier CAN either be a resource identifier or a client idempotency token" -- and SourceAssetTemplateIdentifier is a resource identifier, unique across entries and echoed in this entry's error. Idempotency is structural rather than token-based: an asset id is derived from (CampaignId, SourceAssetTemplateId), so a replayed entry resolves to the same asset (I-16).

SourceAssetTemplateId.documentation: The failing entry's request identifier, so a caller can match this error to the entry it sent.

Code.documentation: Error code -- ResourceNotFoundException when the blueprint is not on the campaign's bound template, InternalServerException otherwise. Throttling never appears here: DG throttles per operation, so a throttle fails the whole batch.

BatchCreateCampaignAssetError.documentation: Why one entry could not be instantiated.

Entries.documentation: The blueprints to instantiate, one entry each.

BatchCreateCampaignAssetRequest.documentation:
Input for BatchCreateCampaignAsset operation.

DG-038: replaces CreateCampaignAssetRequest. Selecting assets is a set decision -- a partner picks which of the bound campaign template's blueprints this campaign will carry -- so the operation takes a list of entries and there is no singular create. "Add the blueprint I skipped" is a batch of one.

Errors.documentation: One entry per blueprint that could not be instantiated. Empty, never absent, when all entries succeeded.

Successful.documentation: One entry per asset that exists as a result of this call, whether created here or already present.

BatchCreateCampaignAssetResponse.documentation:
Output for BatchCreateCampaignAsset.

Per-entry, per AWS Batch Operations. Errors is required and is empty rather than absent on a fully successful call; Successful is the success list the standard makes optional, and DG returns it because a client otherwise cannot learn the ids that were created.

Status is 200 whenever entries were processed individually -- including when every entry failed, since the batch itself succeeded and the entries did not. A 4xx means the batch could not be attempted as a whole and nothing was written.

A partial batch is a real state and the recovery is to re-send the same entry list: an entry is idempotent by identity (I-15/I-16), so what landed no-ops and what did not gets created. An already-existing asset is therefore a Successful row, not an error -- were it an error, a client looping until Errors is empty would never terminate.

Id.documentation: The asset's identifier, derived from (CampaignId, SourceAssetTemplateId) rather than minted, so the same entry always resolves to the same id.

Layout.documentation: For a multi-layout blueprint, the asset's layout options, so a client can render the first layout picker without reading each asset back. Nothing is selected at creation. Absent for a single-layout blueprint.

BatchCreateCampaignAssetResult.documentation: One asset that exists as a result of this call.

State.documentation: The campaign's state, derived on every read from EndOn and its assets. See CampaignState.

CampaignTemplateId.documentation: The campaign template this campaign draws its assets from. Set at create, immutable.

Language.documentation: The language the campaign's assets are written and typeset in: its template's LanguageCode, set at create. To work in another language, create the campaign from that language's template.

PartnerProfile.documentation: The partner's branding — display name, website and logo — from their AWS Partner Central profile, rendered onto every asset of this campaign. Read-only here: the partner edits it in Partner Central, and the next activation or export uses the change. Absent only when the partner has no profile.

SenderEmail.documentation: The address the campaign's emails are sent from. Absent until one is set.

PrivacyPolicyUrl.documentation: The URL of the partner's privacy policy. Absent until one is set.

PartnerAddress.documentation: The partner's postal address. Absent until one is set.

PartnerBadge.documentation: The partner's badge. Absent until one is set, and every badge slot shows the Standalone AWS Partner badge while the partner's primary AWS Partner path is at stage Validated or Differentiated. Below that, no badge is shown.

EmailTarget.documentation: The attached recipient list — metadata only. There is no read path for the addresses.

EmailTargetEngagementGroupIds.documentation: The engagement groups set by CreateCampaign / UpdateCampaign. Absent until set. Resolved to recipients at Start, where the stage can.

SocialConnections.documentation:
The account the campaign's social posts publish from, per platform, as set by UpdateCampaign. Absent until one is set.

Needed only for a platform where you hold two or more connections. With none set, a post uses your one connection on its platform, and fails `SOCIAL_CONNECTION_NOT_CHOSEN` when you hold several. A choice that no longer names a connection on its platform fails `SOCIAL_CONNECTION_MISSING`. Join with `ListSocialConnections` for each connection's status.

EstimatedBudget.documentation: What the partner expects the campaign to cost.

StartOn.documentation: The first day of the campaign's run window.

EndOn.documentation: The last day of the campaign's run window.

ActivationIssues.documentation:
Campaign settings that must be set before the assets listed in each issue can be activated. Empty when nothing is missing.

Each issue names the setting in CampaignSetting — set it with UpdateCampaign — or the profile value in PartnerProfileField — set it in Partner Central — and the assets it blocks in AffectedAssetIds. StartCampaignAssetActivationTask refuses with ValidationException (CAMPAIGN_INCOMPLETE) while a requested asset is affected.

LinkLabel.documentation: DOCUMENT only: the words a page uses for this document, such as "eBook". Fill an AssetLink field's LabelFieldId with it when the partner picks this asset.

State.documentation:
Whether the asset is live.

Reports current truth only, and nothing else on this shape overrides it. During an initial publication it stays INACTIVE until the delivery platform holds the object; during a re-publication it stays ACTIVE, because the previously published content is still serving.

A stopped asset and one never started both read INACTIVE; LastActivationStatus tells them apart, because a stop does not change how the last activation went — stopped is INACTIVE with that member SUCCEEDED, never started is INACTIVE with it absent.

An update never moves this member.

LastActivationStatus.documentation:
How the most recent hand-over to the delivery platform ended.

The hand-over, not the delivery: if DG got the artifact scheduled at the platform this is SUCCEEDED, and whether the platform then delivered is DeliveryStatus. Per category the hand-over point is — email: the mailing armed; social: the create, which is the schedule; landing page: create plus publish-personalisation; document: bytes written.

Read with State this is what separates a stopped asset (INACTIVE with SUCCEEDED here) from one never activated (INACTIVE with this member absent) — a stop does not change how the last activation went.

There is no public UNKNOWN. A hand-over whose outcome DG cannot yet determine reports IN_PROGRESS, because a partner's action is identical either way and there is nothing to do with "unknown". Reporting it as FAILED would be the harmful collapse: that reads as safe to retry, and a retry on an at-most-once create publishes a second live object.

Omitted before the first activation attempt.

DeliveryStatus.documentation:
What the platform did with the artifact after accepting it.

EMAIL and SOCIAL_POST only — absent on every other category, which has no delivery event. See the DeliveryStatus docs.

DeliveryStatusReason.documentation: Why delivery failed. Present only when DeliveryStatus is FAILED. For an email the platform rejected: SENDER_EMAIL_INVALID, RECIPIENT_LIST_EMPTY, MAILING_CREDITS_EXHAUSTED or RECIPIENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Otherwise DELIVERY_FAILED. A Facebook post refused because its connection has no Page is FAILED with SOCIAL_CONNECTION_PAGE_REQUIRED, and withdrawn: reconnect Facebook with a Page selected. A social post the platform stopped retrying, because it could not publish within 12 hours of its scheduled time, is FAILED with DELIVERY_FAILED. Any other social post that could not be published stays PENDING while it is investigated, and is reported FAILED with DELIVERY_FAILED once it is confirmed it will not go out. Deactivate and activate the asset again to retry.

SourceAssetTemplateId.documentation: The asset template this asset was created from: the SourceAssetTemplateIdentifier its BatchCreateCampaignAsset entry named, one of GetCampaignTemplate's CampaignTemplate.AssetTemplates[].Id. Set at create and never writable. Absent on an asset created before DG recorded it, which can't be activated either. A campaign holds at most one asset per asset template, so this is how a client matches a campaign's assets to its template's asset templates, for example to create the same assets in another campaign. Names don't identify one: two asset templates can share a name.

SocialPlatform.documentation: SOCIAL_POST only: the platform the post goes to, set from its template and never writable. The same value CampaignAssetSummary.SocialPlatform reports. Absent for every other category.

FileFormat.documentation: Concrete file format of the finished artifact. For DOWNLOAD_ONLY this is the format of the object export copies through verbatim.

SendMode.documentation: When this asset sends, as chosen with UpdateCampaignAsset. EMAIL and SOCIAL_POST only — the two categories whose delivery platform holds a schedule of its own. Absent until chosen, and then the asset reports SEND_MODE_MISSING.

ScheduledSendAt.documentation:
The send time, present only when SendMode is SCHEDULED. It reaches the delivery platform at the asset's next activation.

Was scheduleDate: UtcDate; retyped with the write member of the same name.

FieldValues.documentation: The asset's pinned template fields — the field schema copied from the blueprint at instantiation, each paired with the partner's current value. Present on every asset instantiated from a blueprint that offers editable fields, whatever its category (design section 3.1); absent on one whose blueprint offers none.

LayoutPreviews.documentation:
The asset's AWS-authored layout, as stable public CDN URLs composed from the fileKeys copied off the blueprint at instantiation. Together with FieldValues this makes the asset self-describing: a client renders the edit form and shows the real layout while editing, with no template lookup.

The stored form is a bare object key and the URL is composed on read. The key is revision-addressed and prior revisions are retained, so the key IS the pin — nothing is copied into the asset bucket, and there is no version parameter to carry (DG-038).

One entry for every category except LANDING_PAGE, which has two and distinguishes them with PageType.

On a multi-layout asset, the SELECTED option's pages only (its first option when none is stored); each option's own previews are on layout.options.

Layout.documentation:
A multi-layout asset's layout choice (DG-044): the selection once made, and every option the asset was created with. Absent for a single-layout asset.

FieldValues is always the union of every option's fields, selected or not, so a client can switch layouts without a round trip: each option lists its own FieldIds. The selection drives layout.selected and the top-level LayoutPreviews only.

ActivationIssues.documentation:
What must be fixed on this asset before it can be activated. Empty when the asset is ready.

Issues don't block saving: an asset can be saved incomplete and fixed over several updates. StartCampaignAssetActivationTask refuses an asset that still has issues: an issue blocks activation when only an edit to the asset can change the outcome. Most issues name the field to fix in FieldId. Fix it with UpdateCampaignAsset, then read this list again.

Besides the issues computed from the asset's content, the list carries what the last activation found: CONTENT_REJECTED and PARTNER_IMAGE_REJECTED when moderation refused a field. Editing that field removes its issue. A CONTENT_REJECTED without a FieldId means the text was refused as a whole; editing any text field removes it.

Problems with the campaign's own settings, such as a missing recipient list, and with the partner's profile, such as a missing logo, are reported on Campaign.ActivationIssues, not here.

PublicUrl.documentation:
The live public address this asset's activation produced.

A landing page's page URL, read back from the delivery platform at activation and preserved across every convergence; a document's public CDN URL, composed on read from the key the publish wrote. Absent until the asset activates, and absent for EMAIL and SOCIAL_POST, which produce no partner-addressable URL of their own.

For a landing page this is the entire deliverable — without it a partner has no way to learn where their live page is. A WIDGET landing page reports none: it is embedded rather than standalone, so absence there is expected rather than a fault.

CampaignAsset.documentation: A marketing asset resource within a campaign.

Status.documentation: This asset's contribution to the task's status.

Reason.documentation: Why the activation did not succeed. Present when status is FAILED.

Message.documentation: A description of Reason for display. Don't parse it. For a mailing-credit shortfall it states the credits needed and remaining.

CampaignAssetActivationOutcome.documentation: How one asset named in a task is going.

CampaignAssetActivationOutcomes.documentation: Per-asset outcomes on a task, at most one per accepted asset.

CampaignAssetActivationStatus.documentation:
How ONE asset's activation is going, inside a task.

Pairs with CampaignAssetActivationTaskStatus: that one is the aggregate, this one is a single asset's contribution to it. Partner Central names its task status per flow rather than sharing one, and this follows that.

Deliberately NOT AttemptStatus, even though the three values coincide today. AttemptStatus is the asset's own attempt axis (LastActivationStatus); this is a per-asset outcome inside a task resource. Identical values do not make two things the same axis, and sharing one enum across unrelated axes means a value added for either appears in the SDK of both. A dedicated enum is additive and safe — do not "simplify" this back.

CampaignAssetActivationTaskId.documentation:
Service-minted activation task identifier: atsk- and 13 characters, from AWS Marketplace's ID Generation Service (DG-082).

The suffix is any 13 ASCII letters or digits, because IDGS's own spec is ambiguous about its charset (DG-092). It refuses an ARN, and it refuses a campaign id, which a client may otherwise mistake for a task id.

CampaignAssetActivationTaskStatus.documentation:
An activation task's status, aggregated over every asset it accepted.

Pairs with CampaignAssetActivationStatus: this is the aggregate, that is one asset's contribution to it.

CampaignAssetCategory.documentation:
The kind of a campaign asset.

Shares its vocabulary with CampaignAssetTemplateType, deliberately: an asset is instantiated from a blueprint and carries the blueprint's kind forward, so two spellings of one concept only ever diverge. LANDING_PAGE, SOCIAL_POST and BANNER_AD were previously WEBPAGE, SOCIAL and VISUAL_AD here while the template side already used these names, and nothing mapped between them.

DG-038 removed VIDEO. Its own comment here recorded why it was the odd one -- "video assets are uploaded rather than instantiated from a blueprint" -- and once BatchCreateCampaignAsset became the only create path, nothing uploads an asset into existence, so the value was unreachable rather than merely unused. The five remaining values correspond one-to-one with CampaignAssetTemplateType, which is what lets the blueprint-to-category mapping be a total switch with no default arm.

CampaignAssetExportFailureCode.documentation: Machine-readable cause of an export task failure. Dedicated to the export flow; see CampaignAssetExportFailureReason.

CampaignAssetExportFailureReason.documentation:
Why a campaign asset export task failed. Present only when the task's status is FAILED.

Dedicated to the export flow — deliberately not the service-wide FailureReason/FailureCode, so export codes are not advertised in the SDKs of unrelated operations. Treat an unrecognised code as an unspecified failure and fall back to message.

CampaignAssetExportTaskId.documentation: Service-minted export task identifier: etsk- and 13 characters, from IDGS (DG-082). The suffix is any 13 ASCII letters or digits, like CampaignAssetActivationTaskId's (DG-092).

CampaignAssetExportTaskStatus.documentation: The state of a campaign asset export task.

Value.documentation: The field's current value; the variant matches the field's type.

CampaignAssetFieldValue.documentation:
One template field on an asset: the schema snapshot taken at instantiation plus the current value. The value is absent while the field is unfilled.

Schema and value are one shape rather than two lists because a client rendering an edit form needs both together, and because the pin (design section 3.1) is what an update validates against — separating them would let values outlive the schema they were checked against.

Addressed by the DG FieldId throughout. The delivery platform's own field-definition ids stay on the template record and are joined in at activation, so a vendor identifier never reaches an asset row or a response (DG-025 containment).

CampaignAssetFieldValueList.documentation: The list of an asset's pinned template fields. Matches the CampaignAssetTemplateFieldList bound — one entry per schema field.

CampaignAssetId.documentation: A campaign asset's id: ast- and 13 lowercase letters or digits (DG-087). An asset has no ARN; it is named by its id within its campaign.

CampaignAssetIdList.documentation: Identifiers of assets on one campaign: those whose output another asset embeds (read-only, derived at creation), or those a campaign-level activation issue blocks. At most 25 — a campaign's kit holds no more blueprints than BatchCreateCampaignAsset instantiates in one call.

CampaignAssetIdentifiers.documentation:
The assets one activation task covers.

Bounded at 25 by derivation rather than by choice: a campaign holds at most one asset per blueprint and a kit holds at most 25 blueprints, so 25 is "every asset this campaign can have" under today's template constraints. Revisit the bound if either changes — raising a limit is backward compatible, lowering one is not.

A list of bare identifiers, not of structures. There is no per-asset input left to carry: the send time belongs to UpdateCampaignAsset. Note the forward cost being accepted — adding a per-asset member later is backward compatible only if the list is of structures, so if a second per-asset input is ever proposed, this is the line to revisit.

CampaignAssetImageSource.documentation: An image stored on one of your assets, named by the field that holds it.

Selected.documentation: The selected option's value. An asset is created with its first option selected; an asset created before that rule, with none stored, reports and activates its first option.

Options.documentation: Every option the asset was created with, in authored order.

CampaignAssetLayout.documentation: A multi-layout asset's layout choice: the selection, when made, and its options.

FieldIds.documentation: The fields this option uses: the FieldValues that stay in scope when it is selected. Lets a client show an option's form before selecting it.

CampaignAssetState.documentation:
The lifecycle position of a campaign asset.

Answers exactly one question — is the asset live — and reports current truth only. The evaluations about the asset are separate members: LastActivationStatus for how the last hand-over to the delivery platform ended, and DeliveryStatus for the send. No member's value depends on another's, so there is nothing to rank.

State rather than Status, and narrowing this enum is what earns the name rather than putting it at risk. The AWS Common Terms test for State is whether a resource exposes "two or more resource attributes, one of which may refer to status" — and CampaignAsset now exposes exactly that shape: State beside LastActivationStatus and DeliveryStatus. So this is no longer a lone enum dressed up as a condition; it is the lifecycle position sitting next to the named status attributes, flat rather than nested. Read on its own the member looks like a single attribute and the standard would ask for Status; read on the resource it is the aggregate the standard reserves State for. Same-domain precedent: Amazon Connect Campaigns uses State for a campaign's lifecycle and Status for a job. Recorded for API office hours.

Distinguish a stopped asset from one never started by whether StartedAt is set; StartedAt is never cleared, not even by a stop.

This enum carried five values, IN_PROGRESS and FAILED alongside the two below plus COMPLETED, and all three were removed rather than deprecated.

IN_PROGRESS and FAILED went because a single projected value could not answer "is it live?" — a live asset with a scan in flight and a stopped asset with a scan in flight both projected IN_PROGRESS, and FAILED collapsed the same way, because the projection ranked its inputs by a frozen precedence and precedence discards facts. The fact it discarded was liveness. The three internal axes the projection read now map onto this member plus LastActivationStatus plus one internal-only distinction, with no information lost. See campaign-asset-design.md §2 and §6.

COMPLETED went because it was doing delivery's job: it meant "delivered", which is a delivery outcome and not a lifecycle position. For an email it was exactly DeliveryStatus = DELIVERED, already modelled and already on the asset; for a social post it was unachievable, because this service cannot observe social delivery at all — so half of its stated meaning, "the email was sent, or the post published", was never reachable. The other three startable types have no delivery event whatever. It had no writer and no reader.

Anyone reintroducing a terminal position needs a fact observable for every startable type, which DeliveryStatus explicitly is not — it covers only EMAIL and SOCIAL_POST.

CampaignAssetStateReason.documentation:
Why an asset could not be, or was not, activated or delivered — the one per-asset reason vocabulary: a task outcome's Reason (refused up front or failed during the run), an ActivationIssue's Code, DeactivateCampaignAsset's StateReason, and an asset's DeliveryStatusReason.

Some of these require a change before another attempt can succeed; others are transient and a retry is enough. Treat an unrecognised value as transient and retryable.

LinkLabel.documentation: DOCUMENT only: the words a page uses for this document, such as "eBook". A client listing the candidates for an AssetLink field reads it here, so a preview can update on pick without a fetch.

State.documentation: Where the asset sits in its lifecycle.

LastActivationStatus.documentation: How the last hand-over to the delivery platform ended. Absent before the first activation.

DeliveryStatus.documentation: Whether the platform has delivered the asset.

DeliveryStatusReason.documentation: Why delivery failed. Present only when DeliveryStatus is FAILED. For an email the platform rejected: SENDER_EMAIL_INVALID, RECIPIENT_LIST_EMPTY, MAILING_CREDITS_EXHAUSTED or RECIPIENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Otherwise DELIVERY_FAILED. A Facebook post refused because its connection has no Page is FAILED with SOCIAL_CONNECTION_PAGE_REQUIRED, and withdrawn: reconnect Facebook with a Page selected. A social post the platform stopped retrying, because it could not publish within 12 hours of its scheduled time, is FAILED with DELIVERY_FAILED. Any other social post that could not be published stays PENDING while it is investigated, and is reported FAILED with DELIVERY_FAILED once it is confirmed it will not go out. Deactivate and activate the asset again to retry.

SourceAssetTemplateId.documentation: The asset template this asset was created from. The same value CampaignAsset.SourceAssetTemplateId reports, and absent when it is.

SocialPlatform.documentation: SOCIAL_POST only: the platform the post goes to. Join it with ListSocialConnections' status for that platform to show a post that cannot activate (a connection missing, EXPIRED or PAGE_REQUIRED) before Start is pressed.

StartedAt.documentation: When the asset first went live, set once. Absent if it never has.

FileFormat.documentation: Concrete file format of the finished artifact.

SendMode.documentation: When this asset sends, as chosen with UpdateCampaignAsset. EMAIL and SOCIAL_POST only — the two categories whose delivery platform holds a schedule of its own. Absent until chosen, and then the asset reports SEND_MODE_MISSING.

ScheduledSendAt.documentation:
The send time, present only when SendMode is SCHEDULED. It reaches the delivery platform at the asset's next activation.

Was scheduleDate: UtcDate; retyped with the write member of the same name.

CampaignAssetSummary.documentation: Summary representation of an asset for list operations.

Type.documentation: The kind of asset this blueprint instantiates as.

Label.documentation: Display label; becomes the instantiated asset's name.

Fields.documentation: The editable-field schema, copied and pinned onto each campaign asset at create. Fields the service fills itself are not listed.

PrerequisiteAssetTemplateIds.documentation: The asset templates this one embeds output from, such as an email's landing page. Each must be in the same BatchCreateCampaignAsset request or already an asset on the campaign, else the create is refused PREREQUISITE_ASSET_MISSING; include them when the partner picks this one. Absent when there are none. A link the partner chooses, such as a landing page's download button, is not listed here: it is an AssetLink field and needs nothing at create.

SocialPlatform.documentation: SOCIAL_POST only: the platform an asset made from this blueprint posts to, which the asset reports as SocialPlatform. Fixed by the template, so a client can show which social connection the post needs before it is created. Absent for every other type.

CampaignAssetTemplate.documentation: One asset blueprint inside a campaign template. The id is template-local — an asset template is not a standalone resource and has no ARN.

FieldId.documentation: The field identifier; matches a {{fieldId}} slot in the layout.

Label.documentation: Human-readable name for the field, for display. Authored in the template policy, never derived from the field id or the source layout's field name: the id is a slug (Page_2_Title) and is not meant to be shown to a partner. Absent on fields imported before labels existed.

Description.documentation: What belongs in this field, in English: its role in the asset and what good content for it is (for example "Headline that names the customer and leads with a source-backed statistic"). AWS-authored with the template; never written by a partner. Absent when the template carries none, never empty. Pinned onto the asset with the field, so a corrected description reaches assets created after the correction.

Page.documentation: One-based page number, for paginated layouts (print documents).

Required.documentation:
Whether the field must be filled before the asset can be activated. Derived from DG policy — never inherited from an upstream authoring system.

Required for activation, not for saving: UpdateCampaignAsset accepts partial content and may clear a required field. An unfilled required field appears in the asset's ActivationIssues as REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING, and activation refuses the asset with the same code.

A text field is filled only by a non-blank value, and a rich-text field only by a value with non-blank text; a Placeholder never fills one. An image field is filled by the partner's image or by the template's DefaultValue. A field the campaign fills (CampaignSetting) or the partner's profile fills (PartnerProfileField) is never unfilled on the asset.

Type.documentation: The field kind, with that kind's constraints, placeholder or default.

CampaignSetting.documentation:
The campaign setting this field shows, when it shows one: the partner sets it once on the campaign and every asset displays it. Present only on such fields.

A client shows the field as "Set on the campaign", linking to the campaign, rather than as an input. UpdateCampaignAsset refuses a value for it with FIELD_SET_ON_CAMPAIGN, and on an asset the field carries no value: read it from the named member of GetCampaign's Campaign.

PartnerProfileField.documentation:
The partner-profile value this field shows, when it shows one: the partner's AWS Partner Central profile supplies it, and every asset of every campaign displays it. Present only on such fields.

A client shows the field as "From your Partner Central profile" rather than as an input. UpdateCampaignAsset refuses a value for it with FIELD_FROM_PARTNER_PROFILE. On a read the field carries the partner's resolved value — the logo as its URL, the name and website as text — so a slot renders from this list alone; GetCampaign's Campaign$PartnerProfile carries the same three values.

CampaignAssetTemplateField.documentation: One slot in an asset template's layout: addressing key, placement, and the field kind carrying its own constraints, placeholder or default.

CampaignAssetTemplateFieldList.documentation:
The list of asset template fields. Bounded by the largest UNION a multi-layout asset pins, not by any single layout: an asset created before its layout is chosen pins every layout's fields. Measured 2026-09-28 across the extracted templates:

whitepaper 2 layouts (88 / 101 fields) union 106 ebook 2 layouts (100 / 78) union 102 solution brief 4 layouts (27-36) union 42 case study 4 layouts (19-23) union 25

A union only grows: a new layout, or an agency adding fields to an existing one, raises it. 150 leaves ~40% headroom over the largest. It was 60 (sized to one 52-field eBook), which refused every whitepaper option. If a template's union approaches this, raise it before importing — a breach passes import and then fails at instantiation.

CampaignAssetTemplateIdList.documentation: Identifiers of asset templates within one campaign template.

CampaignAssetTemplateList.documentation: The list of asset templates. Bounded to the synchronous-instantiation ceiling: templates are platform-curated kits, not partner data.

CampaignAssetTemplateType.documentation: The kind of asset an asset template instantiates as.

CampaignId.documentation: A campaign's id: camp- and 13 letters or digits, from AWS Marketplace's ID Generation Service (DG-082).

CampaignIdentifier.documentation: A campaign, named by its id or its ARN.

CampaignSetting.documentation: A campaign setting, named by its Campaign member: one an asset field shows, or one an asset needs before it can activate (ActivationIssue$CampaignSetting).

CampaignSocialConnectionIds.documentation: The connections chosen for one platform. Exactly one: a social post publishes from one account.

CampaignSocialConnections.documentation: The connection a campaign's social posts publish from, keyed by platform. A map so that each platform appears once.

CampaignSort.documentation: How to order ListCampaigns. Ties break by campaign id, ascending.

CampaignState.documentation:
A campaign's state, derived on every read from its EndOn and its assets:

  1. COMPLETED once the UTC date is after EndOn (so a campaign ending today completes at the next UTC midnight). A campaign with no EndOn never completes, and cannot activate until it has one;
  2. otherwise ACTIVE when any of its assets is ACTIVE;
  3. otherwise DRAFT, including a campaign with no assets.

A summary of the assets, not a lifecycle: nothing transitions it, it is never stored, and it gates no operation by itself: the refusal on a completed campaign (CAMPAIGN_COMPLETED) reads the same EndOn. Otherwise whether an asset can be edited, activated or deleted depends on that asset. So a scheduled email counts as ACTIVE once armed, before it sends; a campaign stays DRAFT during its first activation; deactivating its only active email or social post returns it to DRAFT; and a COMPLETED campaign can still have live landing pages.

CampaignStateList.documentation: States to filter on; a campaign matches if its state is any of them.

Arn.documentation: The campaign ARN. Present on the summary so a caller can tag a campaign straight from a list result without a GetCampaign per row — the same reason the audit timestamps are here.

State.documentation: The campaign's state, derived on every read from EndOn and its assets. See CampaignState.

Language.documentation: The language the campaign's assets are written and typeset in. See Campaign$Language.

StartOn.documentation: The first day of the campaign's run window.

EndOn.documentation: The last day of the campaign's run window.

CreatedAt.documentation: Creation timestamp. Present on the summary so a caller can order a list by recency without reading each campaign in full.

UpdatedAt.documentation: Last update timestamp. Present on the summary for the same reason as CreatedAt.

CampaignSummary.documentation: Summary representation of a campaign for list operations.

UseCase.documentation: Campaign use case for filtering or categorization.

Description.documentation: A short overview of the campaign, as plain text in the template's language: no HTML and no character entities. Absent when the template has none; never an empty string.

LanguageCode.documentation: Language the template is authored in, which a campaign created from it takes. A template has one language; the same content in another language is another template.

Collection.documentation: The browsing context the template is listed in. Every template has exactly one.

CustomerSegments.documentation: The customer segments the template is written for. Absent when the template names none, in which case it matches every CustomerSegments search filter.

Themes.documentation: The template's marketing themes. Absent when the template names none, in which case it matches every Themes search filter.

EffectiveDateBegin.documentation: The instant the template becomes available to partners. Until then the template does not exist to a partner: SearchCampaignTemplates omits it and GetCampaignTemplate returns ResourceNotFoundException.

AssetTemplates.documentation: The ordered asset blueprints. One call serves both template browsing and server-side copy-at-create.

ReferenceMaterials.documentation:
The template's reference materials: guides, briefs, copy blocks and other files a partner downloads and uses in their own channels. Kept apart from AssetTemplates because none of them can become a campaign asset — they have no editable field and nothing to activate — and listing them beside the blueprints invited a BatchCreateCampaignAsset that could only fail.

Absent when the template has none.

CampaignTemplate.documentation: A platform-managed campaign template — an AWS-authored kit of asset blueprints a partner creates a campaign from.

CampaignTemplateCollection.documentation: Which browsing context a campaign template belongs to. A classification of the template, not a resource: it decides where a client lists the template and grants nothing. Every partner may read and use a template in any collection. Clients must tolerate values added later.

CampaignTemplateCollectionFilterList.documentation: The collection facet. Values are OR-ed; exact match.

CampaignTemplateDescription.documentation: A campaign template's overview: plain text in the template's language. The 300-character cap keeps template cards even. The importer refuses a longer one rather than truncating it.

CampaignTemplateId.documentation: A campaign template's id. A campaign template has no ARN and is not an IAM resource type: its operations are action-only (DG-084). So an id is the only way to name one, and an ARN, or any value with : or /, is refused as an invalid id. tmpl- and 13 lowercase letters or digits (DG-088).

UseCase.documentation: Campaign use case for filtering or categorization.

LanguageCode.documentation: Language the template is authored in. See CampaignTemplate$LanguageCode.

Collection.documentation: The browsing context the template is listed in. See CampaignTemplate$Collection.

CustomerSegments.documentation: The customer segments the template is written for. See CampaignTemplate$CustomerSegments.

CampaignTemplateSummary.documentation: Summary representation of a campaign template, returned by search.

ClientToken.documentation:
Idempotency token for mutating operations.

Printable ASCII 33-126 — no spaces, no control characters — per the AWS Idempotency Standard. Never `@required`: a caller that does not need replay protection omits it.

ResourceId.documentation: The affected resource identifier. For a uniqueness conflict this is the identifier of the existing resource, so the caller can act on it without a separate lookup.

Reason.documentation:
Machine-readable cause, for clients that branch on it.

An open set of SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE tokens, deliberately typed as a string rather than an enum. ConflictException is shared by every resource in this service, so an enum here would accumulate values that are meaningful for one resource and inapplicable to the rest — the cohesiveness problem the Backward Compatibility standard describes under "Sharing enums" — and each new value would force an SDK regeneration on callers who can never encounter it. Clients MUST treat an unrecognised value as an unspecified conflict and fall back to Message.

Values in use today:

From the campaign asset activation path. Every one of these is decided before the operation returns, so a caller that receives one knows nothing was started.

These two are thrown by DeactivateCampaignAsset, which refuses one asset outright. StartCampaignAssetActivationTask reports the same two causes per asset as a FAILED task entry instead of throwing, because one bad identifier must not refuse the twenty-four good ones beside it — so the spellings are deliberately identical to CampaignAssetStateReason's, letting a client match one string whichever way the refusal arrived. The two types evolve independently on purpose: this is an open string shared by every resource, that is a closed enum owned by one operation.

  • ASSET_START_IN_PROGRESS — the asset is already being started, or another caller changed it during this request. Retryable once the outcome is visible.
  • PREREQUISITE_ASSET_NOT_ACTIVE — this asset embeds output from another asset that is not live. ResourceId carries that asset's identifier.

From the prerequisite edges between a campaign's assets — an email that embeds its landing page's URL. Both refuse the whole request and write nothing.

  • PREREQUISITE_ASSET_MISSING — from BatchCreateCampaignAsset: an entry's blueprint embeds another blueprint's output, and that blueprint is neither named in the same request nor already an asset on the campaign. Retry with it in the request. ResourceId carries the missing blueprint's identifier.
  • ASSET_HAS_DEPENDENTS — from DeleteCampaignAsset: another asset on the campaign embeds this asset's output, so deleting it would leave that asset unactivatable. Delete the dependents first. The message names them.

CAMPAIGN_COMPLETED — the campaign is complete (the UTC date is after its EndOn), so it and its assets are read-only. Refuses UpdateCampaign, BatchCreateCampaignAsset, UpdateCampaignAsset, DeleteCampaignAsset and StartCampaignAssetActivationTask; never DeactivateCampaignAsset. Not retryable, and not fixable — EndOn cannot be moved once it has passed, so nothing the caller does will make the write succeed. ResourceId carries the campaign identifier.

⚠️ This is the one conflict reason whose condition never clears, which sits awkwardly with ConflictException promising a state that may change. It is a conflict rather than a validation failure because the request is well formed and would have succeeded a moment earlier — the resource's state is what refuses it, which is what this exception is for. Contrast ASSET_NOT_STARTABLE, which moved to ValidationException precisely because it is a property of the asset's type rather than of its state.

⚠️ COMPLETED also exists as a CampaignAssetExportTaskStatus value, on a different axis. That one means an export archive finished assembling. The two are unrelated and must not be unified.

CAMPAIGN_HAS_ACTIVE_ASSETS — from DeleteCampaign: at least one of the campaign's assets is live, and deleting the campaign would orphan what the delivery platform still serves or sends. Deactivate those assets with DeactivateCampaignAsset, then retry. The message names them. ResourceId carries the campaign identifier.

CAMPAIGN_ACTIVATION_IN_PROGRESS — from StartCampaignAssetActivationTask and DeleteCampaign, refusing the whole request: one activation task runs on a campaign at a time. ResourceId carries the holding task's id, so a caller can poll GetCampaignAssetActivationTask rather than guess. Retryable once that task reaches a terminal status.

SERVICE_LINKED_ROLE_DELETION_IN_PROGRESS — from StartCampaignAssetActivationTask, refusing the whole request: this service's service-linked role is being deleted, so no asset may go live. Not a lease conflict: ResourceId is unset and there is no task to poll. Retryable after a short wait; if the role was deleted, the next activation recreates it.

LAYOUT_LOCKED_AFTER_ACTIVATION — from UpdateCampaignAsset, refusing a Layout change on a multi-layout asset that has activated successfully at least once (DG-044). The published object is that layout's, so switching would leave the asset describing a layout that is not the one live. Not fixable: the asset keeps its layout for life. A failed activation does not lock it. Re-sending the layout already selected is not a change and is accepted. ResourceId carries the asset identifier.

ASSET_START_IN_PROGRESS — also from UpdateCampaignAsset, refusing any edit to an asset the campaign's running activation task has accepted and not yet finished: the run publishes the content it read, so an edit accepted mid-run would either be published unvalidated or never published. Nothing is written. Retryable once the asset's outcome on the task (GetCampaignAssetActivationTask) is terminal; the asset's siblings may still be running. ResourceId carries the asset identifier.

ASSET_ALREADY_ACTIVE — from UpdateCampaignAsset, refusing any change to a live email or social post, content or schedule. Deactivate it first; the next activation sends everything current. Landing pages and documents are edited live and converge by re-activation. ResourceId carries the asset identifier.

ASSET_NOT_DEACTIVATABLE — from DeactivateCampaignAsset, for an asset that can't be stopped: a document, banner or landing page until the campaign has completed, when it becomes removable. Until then, update it and activate it again. ResourceId carries the asset identifier.

ASSET_HAS_LOCKED_SENDS — from DeactivateCampaignAsset, within an hour of the asset's send (a social post's publish), when it can no longer be withdrawn. ASSET_ALREADY_DELIVERED — the same, once that time has passed: a sent email or a published post cannot be recalled. Neither is retryable.

Three values were removed with the campaign lifecycle and the singular activate, and none should be re-added here:

  • CAMPAIGN_NOT_STARTED — a campaign has no state to be started out of.
  • ASSET_NOT_STARTABLE — moved to ValidationException, with no reason. The value's own documentation said it was "not retryable and not fixable: it is a property of the asset's type", and ConflictException promises a state that may change. The gate itself stays — deleting it lets a download-only asset into a task with no dispatch arm, which would succeed and do nothing.
  • ASSET_START_UNCONFIRMED — described a state that no longer occurs. DG cannot be more idempotent than a platform whose social create has no idempotency key, so an ambiguous hand-over is now an ordinary failure carrying INTERNAL_ERROR. Holding the asset in a distinct state bought a guarantee that was never real, and had no exit.

ConflictException.documentation: The request conflicts with the current state of the resource.

ConflictReason.documentation: Machine-readable conflict cause. See ConflictException$Reason for the values in use and why this is an open string rather than an enum.

CountryCodeList.documentation:
List of target countries.

Countries and not regions on the wire: a region is a console-side grouping, so the console expands its NAMER / EMEA / APJ / LATAM pickers into member countries before calling. Putting both on the contract would let a caller send a region and a country that disagree, with no rule for which wins.

CampaignTemplateId.documentation:
The campaign template this campaign draws its assets from.

Binds the campaign to a single source template: every asset must come from this template's asset templates, and one from another template is refused at `BatchCreateCampaignAsset`. Immutable once set. Every campaign has one: a campaign's language and its assets' blueprints both come from its template.

Templates are AWS-authored and read-only — they are discovered through `SearchCampaignTemplates` and `GetCampaignTemplate`, and there is no create, update or delete operation for one.

The template's id only: a campaign template has no ARN (DG-084). The member keeps the `Id` name, which is the convention for referencing another resource from a body.

SenderEmail.documentation:
The address every email of this campaign is sent from.

Printable ASCII only, with no spaces or line breaks, or field code `PATTERN_MISMATCH`. Then three rules, all checked when the sender is set. Its domain must exactly match, ignoring case, the domain of the partner's alliance lead email in AWS Partner Central (a subdomain does not), or field code `SENDER_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLIANCE_LEAD`. Then, for a sender at example.com, DNS must hold the CNAME `dkim._domainkey.example.com` → `dkim._domainkey.md02.com` (field code `SENDER_DOMAIN_DKIM_MISSING`) and a DMARC record, one TXT `_dmarc.example.com` starting `v=DMARC1` with a `p` of `none`, `quarantine` or `reject` (field code `SENDER_DOMAIN_DMARC_MISSING`). Both DNS codes are reported together when both records are missing.

A partner who can't satisfy them can't set a sender, so can't run email campaigns. A shared mail provider's domain, such as gmail.com, can't carry the records. Optional here: a campaign with no sender can be created and edited, but its email assets cannot be activated until one is set.

PrivacyPolicyUrl.documentation: The URL of the partner's privacy policy, linked from every email and landing page footer. Optional here: a campaign whose emails or landing pages show it cannot activate them until one is set.

PartnerAddress.documentation: The partner's physical postal address, shown in every email footer and as a landing page's contact line. Optional here: an email that shows it cannot activate until one is set. A landing page that shows it publishes it empty when it is unset, and a document's footer then prints the partner's name alone.

PartnerBadge.documentation:
The partner's badge — a tier or designation badge from AWS Partner Badge Manager — shown in every badge slot of the campaign's emails, landing pages and documents. Optional: until one is set, every badge slot shows the Standalone AWS Partner badge.

A PNG or JPEG of at most 2 MB, staged like an asset image and checked the same way: it must have passed the staging scan (`SCAN_REJECTED`, or `SCAN_IN_PROGRESS` while it is pending), and its bytes must be the format its name says (`IMAGE_FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED`). Any shape is accepted: a badge is drawn whole, never cropped. Content moderation judges it when an asset that shows it is activated.

EmailTarget.documentation:
The campaign's send audience — a CSV of recipient email addresses.

The campaign's *target*: who the campaign is sent to, as distinct from a `CampaignAsset`, which is the content that is sent. It sits on the campaign and not on the activation call because a partner assembles it in the same wizard flow that sets the name and the dates — and because attaching it here means it is validated, staged and resolved to a count before anything is activated, rather than at the last click.

Required format: a header row naming the email column `Email`, `E-mail`, `Email Address` or `E-mail Address` — compared without case, spaces or punctuation. Other columns are permitted and ignored, and with two email columns the first is used. A file without such a header is refused with field code `EMAIL_COLUMN_MISSING`: the address column is never guessed. The rows reach the delivery platform's importer as the partner wrote them — a partner's audience is never rewritten.

At most 5 MB, checked against the object's size before anything is copied, and at most 10,000 distinct addresses, refused with `RECIPIENT_LIST_TOO_LARGE`. A file with no valid address at all is refused with `RECIPIENT_LIST_EMPTY`; otherwise rows without a usable address are not a refusal: they are skipped and counted, and `GetCampaign` reports the counts. Optional here, because a campaign is a container and holds no state to be incomplete in — but an email asset cannot be activated without it, so the requirement moved to the point of activation.

Editable at any time, and an edit reaches the delivery platform only when an asset is activated after it. Each email activation loads the audience into a contact list of its own, so an address taken off the file is not sent to by the next activation.

The bytes are write-only. No response returns a URL or an `S3Uri` for this file; `GetCampaign` returns the scan verdict, when the list was attached and how its rows resolved, and nothing more.

EmailTargetEngagementGroupIds.documentation:
Engagement groups whose contacts the campaign's emails will also go to: the Ids ListEngagementGroups returns (AWS Partner Central Selling). 1–10, each named once.

Each group is named once: a repeated id is refused with field code `INVALID_VALUE`. Not checked against your groups when saved. StartCampaignAssetActivationTask resolves them to recipients. On a stage that can't resolve groups yet, Start refuses an email while groups are set (`ENGAGEMENT_GROUPS_UNAVAILABLE`), rather than send to `EmailTarget` alone.

TargetAudience.documentation: Advisory targeting metadata. Refined later, and not validated here.

EstimatedBudget.documentation: What the partner expects the campaign to cost.

StartOn.documentation: The first day of the campaign's run window. Not after EndOn (ValidationException, INVALID_VALUE).

EndOn.documentation:
The last day of the campaign's run window, inclusive and in UTC. Not in the past: the campaign completes at the UTC midnight after it (see CampaignState). A scheduled send must fall on or before it.

Optional here, but required before any asset activates: until it is set, GetCampaign's ActivationIssues reports END_ON_MISSING and StartCampaignAssetActivationTask refuses (CAMPAIGN_INCOMPLETE). Set it with UpdateCampaign.

ClientToken.documentation: Idempotency token. Same token within 24h returns existing resource.

Tags.documentation:
Tags to apply at creation.

Tag-on-create rather than create-then-tag is a Tagris requirement, not a convenience: it is what lets a tag-based access control policy govern the creation itself. A campaign created untagged and tagged a moment later is briefly outside any such policy.

A key beginning `aws:` (any case) is reserved for AWS-applied system tags and is refused with `ValidationException`, as is a key repeated in the list; nothing is created. The tags are recorded before the campaign is written, so a create that cannot record them fails and creates nothing. A retry with the same `ClientToken` returns the campaign the first attempt created and does not re-apply tags — use `TagResource` to change them afterwards. `ListTagsForResource` returns them.

CreateSocialConnectionAuthorizationUrlRe.documentation:
Input for CreateSocialConnectionAuthorizationUrl.

Names a platform, not a connection: the same call serves a first connect, connecting another account, and re-authorizing an expired one. Which of those it was is decided by the account the partner consents with, and shows up in ListSocialConnections afterwards. Writes nothing in this service.

AuthorizationUrl.documentation: Fresh single-use URL the partner visits to grant authorization.

CustomerSegment.documentation: The customer segment a campaign template is written for. Clients must tolerate values added later.

CustomerSegmentFilterList.documentation: The customer-segment facet. Values are OR-ed; exact match.

CustomerSegmentList.documentation: The customer segments a campaign template is written for.

State.documentation: The asset's lifecycle position — INACTIVE once the stop is confirmed.

LastActivationStatus.documentation: How the most recent activation attempt ended, which a stop does not change. Read with state, it is what separates a stopped asset (INACTIVE + SUCCEEDED) from one never activated (INACTIVE, this member absent). Omitted until a first activation has been attempted.

StateReason.documentation: Why the asset sits where it does. Present when LastActivationStatus is FAILED, or on a deliberate INACTIVE.

DeactivateCampaignAssetResponse.documentation:
Output for DeactivateCampaignAsset.

Synchronous, so the outcome of the stop is this response — there is no lastDeactivationStatus, and its absence is not an oversight. Activation is asynchronous and its outcome arrives long after the response, which is why that one has to be persisted where a partner can read it later.

Identifier.documentation: Identifier or ARN of the social connection to delete.

DeliveryStatus.documentation:
What the delivery platform did with an artifact it accepted.

Distinct from `LastActivationStatus`, which reports the hand-over *to* the platform. Once DG has the mailing armed, the hand-over `SUCCEEDED`; whether the platform then delivered is this member's business, and the two genuinely diverge — `LastActivationStatus = SUCCEEDED` with `DeliveryStatus = FAILED` is an ordinary combination, not a contradiction.

**EMAIL and SOCIAL_POST only.** Landing pages and documents have no delivery event at all.

`PENDING` until the platform shows the outcome. An email is `DELIVERED` once the platform reports it sent, and `FAILED` when the platform reports the send failed. A social post is `DELIVERED` once the platform has published it. A social post is never reported `FAILED` by an observation alone, because the platform retries a failed post. A send that has not resolved a day after its scheduled time stays `PENDING` while it is investigated, and is reported `FAILED` only if it will not go out. A `FAILED` asset can be deactivated and activated again to retry. See campaign-asset-design.md section 6.4.

ScanStatus.documentation: The scan verdict for the attached list.

ValidCount.documentation: Distinct usable addresses — the recipients an email activation sends to.

RejectedCount.documentation: Rows skipped because their email cell is not a usable address.

DuplicateCount.documentation: Rows repeating an address already counted. Not an error: each address is sent to once.

FileName.documentation: The display name of the uploaded file, as the partner named it, with no path: for example Q4 leads.csv. Absent for a list attached before the service kept the name. There is no link to the file: the list is never downloadable from the campaign.

EmailTargetDetail.documentation:
The campaign's attached recipient list, as read — metadata only.

No URL and no `S3Uri`, presigned or otherwise. The file is a list of email addresses belonging to people who are not the partner, so there is no read path for the bytes at all; what a caller needs is whether the list was accepted and how many recipients it resolved to.

The three counts describe the file as it was read when attached. They are absent for a list attached before the service began reading lists at upload.

EngagementGroupId.documentation: An engagement group's id, as ListEngagementGroups (AWS Partner Central Selling) returns it: eng-grp- and 14 lowercase alphanumerics. The same constraints as the Leads model's GroupId, whose pattern pins only the current shape: if Leads relaxes it, so does this.

RichText.documentation: A field whose value is a constrained HTML fragment.

AssetLink.documentation: A link to another asset on the same campaign. The partner chooses which asset, by LinkedAssetId; at activation DG writes that asset's public URL into the field. A landing page's download button is one, naming a DOCUMENT.

FieldType.documentation:
The kind of a template field, carrying that kind's constraints, placeholder or default. One discriminator instead of a separate kind enum, constraints blob and preset value, so kind and constraints cannot disagree. Read-only — templates are AWS-authored; the service validates each partner value against it.

A URL the partner types is not a distinct kind: it is text with a URL pattern, and its link role is carried by the layout placeholder. The same holds for a colour, which is text with a hex-colour pattern. A link to another of the campaign's assets, whose URL DG writes at activation, is AssetLink.

FieldId.documentation: The field to update; must match a FieldId in the asset's stored schema.

Value.documentation: The new value. Omit to clear the field.

FieldValueInput.documentation: A value-only update to one email template field. The write counterpart of CampaignAssetFieldValue: it carries just the addressing key and the new value, never the service-owned schema.

FieldValueInputList.documentation: The list of field value inputs on a write. Matches the CampaignAssetTemplateFieldList bound — at most one entry per schema field.

FileFormat.documentation:
Concrete file format of a rendered or downloadable artifact.

DG-030 added HTML and IMAGE so one enum covers both the download-only office formats and the formats the service renders itself. Before that, an asset carried an ad-hoc HTML | PDF and a template entry an ad-hoc HTML | PDF | IMAGE, and the two disagreed with each other.

VersionId.documentation: The version of the object to take: the VersionId the staging upload returned.

FileRef.documentation:
A reference to a partner-supplied file in the Partner Central file staging bucket.

The URI must be `s3://{stagingBucket}/{callerAccountId}/…`, where the account id segment equals the caller's session-derived account — never an account named in the request body. A mismatch is refused `FILE_REFERENCE_NOT_OWNED`; any other bucket, `FILE_REFERENCE_INVALID`.

`VersionId` is required: the staging bucket is versioned, and the service takes exactly the version the upload returned, so a later upload to the same key cannot change what was referenced. The service copies that version into storage it controls and pins the copy for scanning and processing.

FileReference.documentation:
Opaque reference to an uploaded file.

Sized for the read form as well as the write form: an image field's value comes back as a presigned URL, and one signed with session credentials is ~1,400 characters.

CampaignIdentifier.documentation: The campaign whose current task to read. This addresses the task, and also authorizes the call.

CampaignId.documentation: The campaign's id. Canonical: because CampaignIdentifier accepts an id or an ARN, echoing this tells a caller who passed an ARN what the id is. The task's own id is TaskId.

TaskId.documentation: Opaque correlation value for the task. Echoed so a caller can tell the task it started from a later one that superseded it. Never an input: the campaign is what addresses a task, because a campaign has at most one.

TaskStatus.documentation: The task's status over every asset it names, refused ones included: one refused and one succeeded is PARTIAL_FAILURE.

EndedAt.documentation: When the task reached a terminal status. Absent while IN_PROGRESS.

Assets.documentation: One entry per asset the request named, in the order named. An asset refused up front is FAILED from the first response, with its reason.

GetCampaignAssetActivationTaskResponse.documentation: Output for GetCampaignAssetActivationTask: the campaign's most recent task.

CampaignIdentifier.documentation: The campaign that owns the export task. Accepts the campaign id or ARN. Required so the read is authorized on campaign/{CampaignId}; the task must belong to this campaign or the request resolves to not-found.

CampaignAssetExportTaskIdentifier.documentation:
The export task to retrieve: the Id StartCampaignAssetExportTask returned (etsk-…).

An id only. An export task has no ARN: none is returned, recorded or authorized on (the read authorizes on its campaign), so there is no ARN to accept (DG-063 D-35).

GetCampaignAssetExportTaskRequest.documentation:
Input for GetCampaignAssetExportTask.

Takes the catalog, the owning campaign, and the export task identifier. The campaign identifier is required so the operation can be authorized on the task's owning campaign/{CampaignId}: the task is addressable by its id within the caller's partition, but the campaign is not derivable from the task id alone at authorization time.

DownloadUrl.documentation: Presigned GET URL for the ZIP archive. Present only when status is COMPLETED. Freshly minted on each call and short-lived (<=15 minutes).

ExpiresAt.documentation: When DownloadUrl expires. Present only when status is COMPLETED.

FailureReason.documentation: Why the task failed. Present only when status is FAILED.

Identifier.documentation: The campaign template's id. A campaign template has no ARN (DG-084).

CampaignTemplate.documentation: The campaign template, including its asset templates.

HtmlTagName.documentation: An HTML tag name, without angle brackets.

Id.documentation: Opaque identifier for output fields that name a blueprint (a template's asset). Max 64 bytes.

Identifier.documentation:
Opaque resource identifier for input parameters. Accepts id or ARN.

Only the characters an id or an ARN can contain: letters, digits and _:/+=,.@-.

DefaultValue.documentation: The AWS-authored image the asset uses until the partner sets one: shown in previews and published in an empty slot of an email, landing page, banner ad or social post. It fills a required image field. A document leaves an empty image slot blank.

RecommendedWidthPixels.documentation:
