The image size, in pixels, that fills this slot and prints sharply, for example 1920 x 301 for a full-width header. Shown to the partner as "Recommended: W x H px".

Present, together with RecommendedHeightPixels, on document (PDF) image slots only, where the slot is a fixed rectangle. Such a slot is always filled: the image is scaled to cover it, centred, and clipped to it, the same as CSS object-fit: cover. An image whose shape is too far from W:H is refused with IMAGE_ASPECT_RATIO_MISMATCH; one narrower than W is accepted. A slot showing the partner's logo or badge, and a slot without the two members (every slot from before sizes existed), fits the image inside instead (object-fit: contain): a logo or a badge is never cropped. Email and landing-page image slots are laid out by HTML and carry neither.

RecommendedHeightPixels.documentation: The image height, in pixels, that fills this slot. Present exactly when RecommendedWidthPixels is.

IndustryFilterList.documentation: The industry facet. Values are OR-ed; exact, case-sensitive match.

InternalServerException.documentation: An unexpected error occurred during the processing of the request.

LanguageFilterList.documentation: The language facet. Values are OR-ed; exact, case-sensitive match.

LayoutOptionValue.documentation: A layout option's value, as the template authors it (e.g. "OptionA").

LayoutPageType.documentation: Which page of a multi-page layout a preview serves.

Url.documentation: A stable URL serving the object. Not presigned, so it does not expire.

PageType.documentation:
Which page of a multi-page layout this is. Present only for LANDING_PAGE, which genuinely has two layout objects — the page carrying the form, and the confirmation page shown after submit — and absent for every other category, which has one.

A confirmation page is a second LAYOUT, never a second asset: modelling it as its own asset would give it a lifecycle, an activation and a state it does not have.

LayoutPreview.documentation:
A rendering of an AWS-authored layout skeleton or placeholder image.

The url is a stable, cache-friendly CloudFront URL rather than a presigned GET, because the bytes are AWS marketing content that is already public. The key's random segment is the object's only protection, so the URL is a bearer credential for the object and is withheld entirely while a template is not yet effective — see CampaignTemplate.EffectiveDateBegin.

LayoutPreviewList.documentation: The list of layout previews for one asset template.

LayoutUrl.documentation: A URL serving DG-hosted layout or placeholder bytes.

LinkLabel.documentation: How a page names a document it links to, such as "Solution Brief" or "eBook".

CampaignIdentifiers.documentation: Only these campaigns, each named by its id or its campaign ARN. A campaign that does not exist, was deleted, or whose ARN names another account or catalog is left out rather than refused.

Name.documentation: Only campaigns whose name contains this, compared case-insensitively.

States.documentation: Only campaigns in one of these states.

NextToken.documentation: Pagination token. Bound to the filters and sort it was issued for: a request that changes CampaignIdentifiers, Name, States or Sort between pages is refused with ValidationException. MaxResults may change.

ListCampaignsRequest.documentation:
Input for ListCampaigns operation.

Filters combine with AND. Results are eventually consistent: a campaign created, renamed or activated a moment ago can take up to a second to appear with its current values. GetCampaign is strongly consistent.

Platform.documentation: Restrict results to a single social platform.

MaxResults.documentation: Maximum number of results to return per page.

Items.documentation: The social connections for this partner and catalog.

NextToken.documentation: Pagination token for the next page, absent on the last page.

ResourceArn.documentation: The ARN of the resource whose tags should be returned.
The ARN of the resource the tags belong to.

Tags.documentation: The tags currently applied. Absent rather than empty when the resource carries no tags.

MaxResults.documentation: Maximum number of results to return per page.

Amount.documentation: The amount, as a decimal string with at most two decimal places.

CurrencyCode.documentation: The ISO 4217 currency the amount is denominated in.

MonetaryValue.documentation:
An amount of money in a named currency.

The amount is a decimal string, not a float: a budget is exact, and binary floating point cannot represent every two-decimal value. Mirrors the Partner Central Selling API's `ExpectedCustomerSpend.Amount`.

PartnerAddress.documentation:
The partner's physical postal address, as one line of plain text: the sender's address that commercial email must carry (CAN-SPAM in the US, CASL in Canada). A registered post office box or private mailbox counts.

No markup, line break or control character. Shown in the footer of every email, and as the contact line of a landing page.

Sensitive: for a sole trader it is a home address, so it is kept out of logs and CloudTrail events.

Url.documentation: A presigned GET of the badge, which expires one hour after the read: fetch it again with GetCampaign when it returns 403.

PartnerLogoUrl.documentation:
A partner's profile logo URL, as AWS Partner Central serves it.

`https` only: the URL is written into landing pages and email that Partner Central Marketing publishes on the partner's behalf, so a cleartext one would be fetched over the wire by every recipient.

LogoUrl.documentation:
The profile's logo URL, as AWS Partner Central serves it — the image every asset of the campaign shows. Absent when the profile names none.

Partner Central Marketing keeps no copy: the same URL is written into a published landing page and email, and fetched when a document is composed, so what a client renders from it is what is sent. Only a document fetches the image: one it cannot fetch and draw fails that asset with `INTERNAL_ERROR`, which a retry can clear. A landing page or email links the URL as given, so a logo that does not load shows as a broken image.

RefreshedAt.documentation: When this branding was last read from Partner Central. Earlier than the request when Partner Central could not be reached and Partner Central Marketing answered from its last copy.

PartnerProfileBranding.documentation:
A partner's branding, read from their AWS Partner Central profile.

The profile is the only source: a campaign carries no branding of its own, so every campaign of a partner shows the same identity, vetted by Partner Central. Edit it in Partner Central.

PartnerProfileField.documentation: A value of the partner's AWS Partner Central profile that an asset field shows, or that an asset needs before it can activate (ActivationIssue$PartnerProfileField). Each names a member of PartnerProfileBranding.

Platform.documentation: Social platform a connection authorizes publishing on.

PrivacyPolicyUrl.documentation:
The URL of the partner's privacy policy, linked from the footer of every email and landing page of a campaign.

`https` with a host, no user info, the default port, and none of `" ' ( ) < > \` or whitespace: it is written into pages and email that are HTML-decoded downstream, so a quote would break out of the link. The pattern is the first check; the service applies the full rule. Never the website URL: a landing page's form collects leads with the partner as data controller, so the link must be a real privacy policy.

PublicUrl.documentation: A live public address an activation produced — a page at the delivery platform, or a published document on DG's CDN.

Url.documentation: A stable public CDN URL for the file. AWS-authored content, so it is not presigned and carries no expiry — the same treatment as LayoutPreview.url, and withheld on the same condition: absent while the template's EffectiveDateBegin is in the future.

ReferenceMaterial.documentation:
A reference material that comes with a campaign template: a file the partner downloads as-is.

Not a blueprint: it carries no fields, cannot be instantiated, and is not activated.

Not the ReferenceMaterial resource deleted on 2026-09-22 (its six operations, ARN and record are gone). That was partner-uploaded and addressable; this is AWS-authored template content with no identity of its own.

ReferenceMaterialList.documentation:
The reference materials of a template, in the template's display order. An entry has no id, so list order is its only ordering signal: it is meaningful and preserved, and a client should present the list as given rather than sort it.

Platform-curated. Bounded at 30: the largest kit measured (Amazon Quick for SMB, 2026-09-28) carries 21.

MaxLength.documentation: Maximum accepted length of the markup fragment.

AllowedTags.documentation: The HTML tags permitted in the value. Anything else is stripped.

Placeholder.documentation: Example markup shown where the field is empty in a preview of the asset, restricted to AllowedTags. Never the asset's value: it is not set on the asset at create, does not fill a required field, and is never published.

RichTextFieldType.documentation: A rich-text field's constraints and placeholder. Distinct from text because the value is a markup fragment whose permitted tags are part of the contract: a client needs the tag list to configure its editor, and the service needs it to sanitize.

S3Uri.documentation:
An s3:// URI naming a partner-supplied file.

Appears only as a request input. The service never echoes a raw S3 URI back to a caller — a read returns a URL, or for a PII file no location at all.

S3VersionId.documentation: The S3 version id of a referenced object.

ScanStatus.documentation:
The verdict of a file's malware and content-quality scan.

A process with an outcome, not a resource with a lifecycle — hence `Status`. A file is accepted and scanned afterwards, so `PENDING` is a real, observable state rather than an internal one, and it is a refusal at launch rather than something a launch waits on.

Catalog.documentation: The catalog (AWS or Sandbox). AWS and Sandbox templates may differ.

SearchText.documentation: Free-text query matched against the template's name and description. Any word may match, and the last word matches as a prefix when it has 3 or more characters, so nov finds Amazon Nova. A template whose name holds the query as a phrase ranks first, then whole-word matches, then prefix-only ones. Omit to browse the whole catalog. Text analysis is derived from each template's own LanguageCode, never from the language filter.

Industry.documentation: Restrict to templates in these industries. Values within this member are OR-ed; distinct facet members are AND-ed. Exact, case-sensitive match.

UseCase.documentation: Restrict to templates with these campaign use cases. Values within this member are OR-ed; distinct facet members are AND-ed. Exact, case-sensitive match.

Language.documentation: Restrict to templates in these language(s), matched by each template's LanguageCode. Values within this member are OR-ed; distinct facet members are AND-ed. Narrows results; it does not reinterpret SearchText.

AwsServices.documentation: Restrict to templates promoting these AWS services. Values within this member are OR-ed; distinct facet members are AND-ed. Exact, case-sensitive match.

CustomerSegments.documentation: Restrict to templates for these customer segments. Values within this member are OR-ed; distinct facet members are AND-ed. A template that names no customer segment matches every value.

Themes.documentation: Restrict to templates with these themes. Values within this member are OR-ed; distinct facet members are AND-ed. A template that names no theme matches every value.

Collection.documentation: Restrict to templates in these collections. Values within this member are OR-ed; distinct facet members are AND-ed. Omit for no restriction; there is no default.

TotalResults.documentation: Total count over the whole matching set, not just this page — for "over N results" display.

SenderEmail.documentation:
The address a campaign's emails are sent from.

Its domain — everything after the `@` — must exactly match, ignoring case, the domain of the partner's alliance lead email in AWS Partner Central, and must hold the DKIM and DMARC records `CreateCampaign` names. A subdomain does not match. The shape checks only that there is one `@` with printable-ASCII text either side; the domain and DNS checks are the service's.

Printable ASCII, not "anything but whitespace": this becomes the From header of every email the campaign sends, and `\\s` is ASCII-only, so it would admit Unicode separators such as U+2028. Nothing real is lost — Partner Central's lead email and DNS names are ASCII, so a non-ASCII domain could never match.

Sensitive: often a person's address, so it is kept out of logs and CloudTrail events.

SocialAccountName.documentation: Display name of the social account behind a connection, as the platform reports it — a handle on X, a member or company name on LinkedIn. The only thing that tells two connections on one platform apart where no Page applies. Sensitive: on LinkedIn it is usually a person's name.

SocialConnectionId.documentation:
Service-generated identifier of a social connection.

Stable for the life of the connection: it survives a revoke and a re-authorization of the same account, and is never reused once the connection is deleted. sc- and 13 lowercase letters or digits (DG-092).

SocialConnectionIdentifier.documentation: A social connection, named by its id or its ARN.

SocialConnectionStatus.documentation:
Authorization state of a social connection.

The execution backend's view, plus one thing it does not report: a Facebook connection with no Page reads active there but cannot post (PAGE_REQUIRED). There is deliberately no "authorizing" value: a connection exists only once consent has completed, so an unfinished consent is simply not in the list.

PageName.documentation: The Facebook Page this connection publishes to. Absent where no Page applies.

AccountName.documentation: Display name of the account behind this connection. Absent when the execution backend reports none.

ConnectedAt.documentation: When the account was last authorized. Advances on every re-authorization.

ExpiresAt.documentation: When the authorization lapses. Absent where the platform reports no expiry (X never does). A connection past this time reads EXPIRED only once the backend notices, so treat this as a warning date, not a status.

SocialConnectionSummary.documentation:
Summary of a social connection returned by ListSocialConnections.

Carries no ARN (owner ruling 2026-10-05): a connection is addressed by its Id. Social connections are not taggable, and every social operation authorizes on its action rather than on a resource ARN.

SocialPageName.documentation: Name of the Facebook Page a connection publishes to.

CampaignIdentifier.documentation: The campaign identifier, which also authorizes the call.

CampaignAssetIdentifiers.documentation: The assets to activate, in any order — the service derives the dependency order and ignores the order given here.

ClientToken.documentation:
Idempotency token. Two requests carrying the same token are one request, and the second returns the first one's task rather than starting a second.

The deduplication window is the life of the task record, not a fixed number of hours: replaying a token after the task has expired starts a new task. Stated because a caller would otherwise assume the usual few-hour guarantee.

CampaignId.documentation: The campaign's id. Canonical: because CampaignIdentifier accepts an id or an ARN, echoing this tells a caller who passed an ARN what the id is. The task's own id is TaskId.

TaskId.documentation: Opaque correlation value for the task. Echoed so a caller can tell the task it started from a later one that superseded it. Never an input: the campaign is what addresses a task, because a campaign has at most one.

TaskStatus.documentation: The task's status over every asset it names, refused ones included: one refused and one succeeded is PARTIAL_FAILURE.

EndedAt.documentation: When the task reached a terminal status. Absent while IN_PROGRESS.

Assets.documentation: One entry per asset the request named, in the order named. An asset refused up front is FAILED from the first response, with its reason.

StartCampaignAssetActivationTaskResponse.documentation: Output for StartCampaignAssetActivationTask: the task just created.

CampaignIdentifier.documentation: The campaign whose assets are exported. Accepts the campaign id or ARN.

ClientToken.documentation: Idempotency token. Two requests carrying the same token within the dedup window are one request and return the same task id.

Status.documentation: The task's state, always IN_PROGRESS at creation.

StartCampaignAssetExportTaskResponse.documentation:
Output for StartCampaignAssetExportTask.

Returns the newly created task id and its status, which is always IN_PROGRESS on this synchronous return. Poll GetCampaignAssetExportTask for the outcome.

Tag.documentation: A key-value pair applied to a resource.

TagKey.documentation:
A tag key.

The aws: prefix is reserved for AWS-applied system tags and is rejected for caller-supplied tags — enforced in the service rather than by this pattern, so the rejection carries a message explaining why rather than a bare constraint violation.

TagKeyList.documentation: A list of tag keys to remove.

TagList.documentation: A list of tags. The bound matches the sibling Partner Central services rather than the 50-tag figure in the general AWS tagging guidance, so that a caller who works across Partner Central services sees one consistent limit.

ResourceArn.documentation: The ARN of the resource to tag.

TagValue.documentation: A tag value. May be empty; a key with no value is a valid tag.

TaggableResourceArn.documentation:
The ARN of a taggable Partner Central Marketing resource.

One resource type is taggable — the campaign:

arn:aws:partnercentral:{region}:{account}:catalog/{Catalog}/campaign/{CampaignId}

Nothing else is taggable, and the pattern admits nothing else. A campaign asset has no ARN at all: every asset operation authorizes on its campaign, and aws:ResourceTag on one resolves the campaign's tags, so an asset tag could never affect access (DG-063 D-20). A social connection has an ARN but is not taggable. Reference materials no longer exist.

{account} is the partner's own account — the caller's — not the service account, mirroring PartnerArnHelper.buildPartnerArn in AWSPartnerEntityService. Both region and account are always populated: Tagris's ArnStateMachineProcessor.getRegionRequirement treats a vendor with no explicit region map as REQUIRED, so an ARN omitting either fails to parse.

Templates are deliberately absent. They are AWS-authored and platform-managed — read-only API surface, no customer account in their partition key, seeded by an internal script — so they fall under the "AWS Service owned resources" exemption rather than being customer-taggable.

The ARN service field is the shared Partner Central family code partnercentral, not this service's partnercentral-marketing facet (which names the endpoint, SigV4 signing name and CloudTrail event source). The pattern follows the sibling Partner Central services (PartnerCentralBenefitsServiceModel, PartnerIntegrationAPIModel), which share that service field.

Campaign is a literal and the id segment excludes /, so no other resource type and no nested form matches. The service's own type check stays as a second line, for a stage that runs without model validation.

TargetAudience.documentation:
Advisory targeting metadata for a campaign.

Describes who the campaign is *about*, and never drives a send — that is `EmailTarget`. Nothing here is validated at create, because a partner refines it across the wizard.

TemplateFieldDescription.documentation: What belongs in a template field, in English. Measured 2026-10-18 across the 286 Build with AI descriptions: longest 273.

TemplateFieldId.documentation:
A field's slot name — the developer-readable key that matches a {{fieldId}} placeholder in the layout skeleton (e.g. "Headline", "CtaUrl"), or the form field name in a document template (e.g. "Page 2 Title"). Platform-assigned and semantic (not a service-generated opaque Id), so it has its own constrained shape rather than reusing Id.

Single spaces between words are allowed because document templates name their fields that way, and this shape is the input type for editing them. Leading, trailing and repeated spaces are not, so that "Title" and "Title " cannot be two different fields.

TemplateFieldIdList.documentation: A list of field ids, bounded like the field lists it indexes.

TemplateFieldLabel.documentation: A template field's display name. Measured 2026-09-30 across beta's 503 stored labels: longest 42.

TemplateFieldPattern.documentation: A regular expression constraining a text field's value.

Text.documentation: Text value — for both text and RichText fields. A RichText value is a markup fragment restricted to the field's AllowedTags.

ImageReference.documentation:
Image reference (image fields).

On a write, one of exactly two forms:

  • the s3:// URI of a file you staged in the Partner Central file staging bucket. It is scanned, then copied into this asset.
  • the URL Build with AI returned for a suggested image, unchanged. It is copied into this asset and not scanned. Any other URL is refused with FILE_REFERENCE_INVALID, including one a read returned: to keep the current image, omit the field; to put it on another asset, use CampaignAssetImage.

On a read, a URL the caller can fetch: an image in the asset's own storage comes back as a presigned GET that expires one hour after the read, so fetch it again with GetCampaignAsset when it returns 403; an image already on DG's public CDN comes back as that stable URL. A stored reference outside this asset's storage, or not a raster image, is never signed, and the value is omitted. The signed URL serves the image as its image type, whatever the upload declared.

LinkedAssetId.documentation: The asset an AssetLink field names: the id of an asset on the same campaign, of the field's category. It is a prerequisite of this asset while linked, so it activates first, this asset cannot start until it is live, and it cannot be deleted.

CampaignAssetImage.documentation: Write only. Copies an image stored on another of your assets into this image field. The image is checked against this field's constraints and not scanned again. Also requires partnercentral:GetCampaignAsset on the source campaign. Reads return the copy as ImageReference.

TemplateFieldValue.documentation: The value of a template field. Exactly one variant is set, matching the field's type: text and RichText fields use text, image fields use ImageReference (or, on a write, CampaignAssetImage), AssetLink fields use LinkedAssetId.

Pattern.documentation: Regular expression the value must match — used for URL, email, phone and hex-colour fields.

Placeholder.documentation: Example text shown where the field is empty in a preview of the asset. Never the asset's value: it is not set on the asset at create, does not fill a required field, and is never published.

Theme.documentation: The marketing theme of a campaign template. Clients must tolerate values added later.

ThemeFilterList.documentation: The theme facet. Values are OR-ed; exact match.

ThemeList.documentation: The marketing themes of a campaign template.

ThrottlingException.documentation: The request was denied due to request throttling.

ResourceArn.documentation: The ARN of the resource to remove tags from.

TagKeys.documentation: The tag keys to remove. Associated values are removed with them.

FieldValues.documentation:
Value-only updates to the asset's pinned template fields, keyed by FieldId. The field schema (labels, descriptions, constraints, placeholders, image defaults) is service-owned and pinned at instantiation, so clients send only the values they are changing. Fields omitted keep their stored values; send the entry with Value omitted to clear one.

Named FieldValues to match the member it edits on CampaignAsset, which is the same concept read back. It was templateFieldUpdates; the two names for one concept were the defect, not the length.

Layout.documentation:
Selects a multi-layout asset's layout: one of the values in CampaignAsset.layout.options.

PATCH: omitted leaves the selection unchanged, and there is no way to clear it. A value that is not one of the asset's options — or any value on a single-layout asset — is a plain ValidationException, and nothing in the call is applied. Every pinned field stays writable whichever layout is selected.

SendMode.documentation:
When a sendable asset (EMAIL, SOCIAL_POST) sends: on activation, or at ScheduledSendAt.

A mode beside a value rather than a union, on purpose: ScheduledSendAt stays a plain Timestamp, and the precedent is EventBridge Scheduler's FlexibleTimeWindow { Mode, MaximumWindowInMinutes }. The pair is checked as one, and a request where they disagree is refused with ValidationException (INVALID_VALUE, naming the member) and applies nothing:

  • SCHEDULED requires ScheduledSendAt; a reschedule resends SCHEDULED with the new time;
  • ON_ACTIVATION forbids ScheduledSendAt, and drops any time already stored;
  • ScheduledSendAt without SendMode is refused.

PATCH: omitted leaves both unchanged. Until a mode is chosen the asset reports SEND_MODE_MISSING and does not activate: no default, because an unchosen send mails the real audience. Rejected with ValidationException (NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR_CATEGORY) for a category that has no send (LANDING_PAGE, DOCUMENT, BANNER_AD). Like every other edit, it reaches the delivery platform at the asset's next activation, and a live email or social post refuses it (ASSET_ALREADY_ACTIVE): deactivate first.

ScheduledSendAt.documentation:
The send time, with SendMode: SCHEDULED and only then. See SendMode.

Must be at least an hour out (SEND_WINDOW_TOO_SOON), unless it is the time already stored: resending the stored mode and time changes nothing and is accepted, so a form that always resubmits does not trip the window.

Must also fall on or before the campaign's EndOn (by the end of that UTC day): refused with ValidationException (INVALID_VALUE) otherwise, so nothing is scheduled to send after the campaign completes.

Was scheduleDate, a YYYY-MM-DD string. Retyped because a date alone cannot express a send time, which is the whole point of a schedule — and because the resource already spelled the same concept ScheduledSendAt on the activation responses. Two spellings of one concept on one resource was the defect.

ClientToken.documentation: Idempotency token. Retry-safety only — this is not a concurrency token, and sequential edits to one field are last-writer-wins.

State.documentation:
The asset's state, unchanged.

An update never moves it, so a live asset stays ACTIVE while its edited values take effect for the next activation. There is no edit-outcome member: a 200 means every submitted value applied, and every failure is a refusal on the call itself (DG-040 Decision 11).

ActivationIssues.documentation:
What must be fixed on this asset before it can be activated. Empty when the asset is ready.

Issues don't block saving: an asset can be saved incomplete and fixed over several updates. StartCampaignAssetActivationTask refuses an asset that still has issues: an issue blocks activation when only an edit to the asset can change the outcome. Most issues name the field to fix in FieldId. Fix it with UpdateCampaignAsset, then read this list again.

Besides the issues computed from the asset's content, the list carries what the last activation found: CONTENT_REJECTED and PARTNER_IMAGE_REJECTED when moderation refused a field. Editing that field removes its issue. A CONTENT_REJECTED without a FieldId means the text was refused as a whole; editing any text field removes it.

Problems with the campaign's own settings, such as a missing recipient list, and with the partner's profile, such as a missing logo, are reported on Campaign.ActivationIssues, not here.

UpdateCampaignAssetResponse.documentation:
Output for UpdateCampaignAsset.

A minimal acknowledgment, not an echo. Read GetCampaignAsset for the applied values (FieldValues).

SenderEmail.documentation:
Sets or replaces the address the campaign's emails are sent from. Checked by the same three rules as on CreateCampaign, with the same codes, but only when it differs, ignoring case, from the stored sender: re-sending the stored one is not checked, and StartCampaignAssetActivationTask re-checks it before an email activates.

Replaces, never clears: like every member of this operation, an omitted value leaves the sender as it was, and there is no way to remove one once set.

PrivacyPolicyUrl.documentation: Sets or replaces the URL of the partner's privacy policy. Replaces, never clears.

PartnerAddress.documentation: Sets or replaces the partner's postal address. Replaces, never clears.

PartnerBadge.documentation: Sets or replaces the partner's badge, checked exactly as on CreateCampaign. Replaces, never clears: upload the Standalone AWS Partner badge to show it again. The badge an asset already published keeps showing on it until that asset is activated again.

EmailTarget.documentation:
Replaces the campaign's attached recipient list.

The referenced object is copied and pinned again on every call that supplies it, so the pinned copy always reflects the *last* `UpdateCampaign` that named one. Editing the source object in your own bucket without calling this operation again has no effect.

Replaces, never detaches: a partner can swap the list but cannot remove it.

EmailTargetEngagementGroupIds.documentation:
Engagement groups whose contacts the campaign's emails will also go to (see CreateCampaign). Replaces the stored list; never clears it.

As on `CreateCampaign`: each group once (`INVALID_VALUE` otherwise), not checked against your groups when saved, and resolved at Start where the stage can (`ENGAGEMENT_GROUPS_UNAVAILABLE` where it can't).

SocialConnections.documentation:
Sets the account the campaign's social posts publish from, per platform. Each platform named replaces that platform's choice; a platform not named keeps its own. Replaces, never clears.

Not checked against your connections here: a connection can be deleted at any time, so the activation checks the choice. See `Campaign$SocialConnections`.

EstimatedBudget.documentation: What the partner expects the campaign to cost.

ClientToken.documentation: Idempotency token. Accepted and not stored: this is a change-only partial update with last-writer-wins, so re-applying the same call produces the same result and the same response. There is nothing a replay cache would protect.

StartOn.documentation: The first day of the campaign's run window. Not after EndOn (ValidationException, INVALID_VALUE).

EndOn.documentation:
The last day of the campaign's run window, inclusive and in UTC.

Editable only while the campaign is open, like everything else here: once the stored EndOn has passed the campaign is completed and this update is refused (CAMPAIGN_COMPLETED). Refused with ValidationException (INVALID_VALUE) when it is in the past, or earlier than the day of a scheduled send on one of the campaign's assets: move or cancel that send first. Setting it to today ends the campaign at the next UTC midnight.

UseCaseFilterList.documentation: The use-case facet. Values are OR-ed; exact, case-sensitive match. A constrained string, not an enum: the use-case taxonomy is not yet enumerated.

UtcDate.documentation:
A UTC calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD.

A date and not a `timestamp` on purpose. The values this carries — a campaign's run window, an asset's send date — are calendar dates a partner picks in a wizard, with no meaningful time-of-day; modelling them as an instant invited callers to send one, which then had to be parsed back out and truncated. The pattern is the whole contract, so an invalid date is rejected at the edge rather than surfacing later as a malformed schedule.

Reason.documentation: The single coarse reason the request was rejected, for a caller that does not care which field.

FieldList.documentation:
Every field that failed, not just the first.

⚠️ **Every field, deliberately.** The convention comment carried by most internal models — *"if more than one field caused the error, pick one and elaborate in the message"* — is the reading this service does NOT take: a partner editing a form would then discover their errors one request at a time. The whole request is validated and the full set reported, so one round of fixes is one call.

Each entry names a member of the request just sent, and only that: the value to change and send again. A template field value is `Name` `FieldValues` with the template field in `FieldId`, one entry per failing field.

When it is present. Only when the refusal points at something the partner fixes in a form, and then every such refusal carries it: - `UpdateCampaignAsset`: `FieldValues` (including a file the content scan declined, which is why a partner handles image failures and text failures the same way, through this list), `Layout`, `SendMode` and `ScheduledSendAt`; - `CreateCampaign` and `UpdateCampaign`: campaign settings and files; - `GetCampaignTemplate`: `Identifier`.

Every other `ValidationException` carries `Message` only — tags, ARNs, social connections, exports, and `CAMPAIGN_INCOMPLETE`, whose missing settings are not members of the request it refuses.

ValidationException.documentation:
The input fails to satisfy the constraints specified by the service.

A caller branches on Reason, and where the rejection is attributable to particular fields it reads FieldList rather than parsing Message, which is prose and may change.

Name.documentation: The member of the request that failed, as the request names it: FieldValues for a template field value, Layout, EmailTarget, Identifier, and so on. It is never a template field id: a template field is always FieldValues, with the field in FieldId.

FieldId.documentation: The template field that failed, when Name is FieldValues; absent otherwise.

Message.documentation: Why this field failed, in prose a partner can be shown directly.

Code.documentation: Why this field failed, as a value a client branches on. Read this rather than Message.

ValidationExceptionFieldCode.documentation:
Why one field was refused.

A modeled enum rather than a free string because a client branches on it — a partner UI highlights the field and picks its own wording, which it cannot do from prose. partnercentralbenefits models its ValidationExceptionField$Code the same way.

ValidationExceptionReason.documentation:
Why the request failed validation, coarsely.

Matches the shape partnercentralbenefits ships (ValidationException$Reason) so a client that already reads one Partner Central API's validation errors reads this one the same way.
